title: Saying who has one thing
summary: Put the possessor first, fixed on next, and one thing in its basic singular form last.
objectives: Say who has one thing using the owner + on + noun pattern.
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Put the possessor first, fixed on next, and one thing in its basic singular form last.

steps: First put minulla in the owner position. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with auto (“car”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put sinulla in the owner position. sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with pallo (“ball”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put hänellä in the owner position. hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Next put on after the owner: “has”.
End with kynä (“pen”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put meillä in the owner position. meillä means “we as the owner”.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with koira (“dog”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put teillä in the owner position. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with kirja (“book”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put heillä in the owner position. heillä means “they as the owner”.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with kissa (“cat”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put minulla in the owner position. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with peli (“game”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put teillä in the owner position. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with tyyny (“pillow”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.

commonMistakes: Begin the requested statement with the owner, then on, then the thing: Minulla on pallo.
Keep the owner form and verb separate: minä names a subject; minulla on says what I have.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses its fixed on form with every owner, including we and they.
pallo stays in its basic singular form: one ball.
